title: Candidate governed Bounded Context and Ownership Model
purpose: Define explicit candidate domain boundaries, ownership traces, ubiquitous language, cross-context contracts, and context-map relationships for accountable review.

boundedContexts.name: Governed Product Core
boundedContexts.purpose: Own governed Product semantics, exact validation, immutable history, assessments, and workspace persistence within one explicit language boundary.
responsibilities: Assess candidate records without granting approval or readiness
Persist validated current records, immutable history, and attributable audit events
excludedResponsibilities: Appoint organizational owners or approve Product architecture
Render host-native interaction or execute external providers

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A versioned, attributable and reviewable Product-domain record that carries no approval, readiness, release, appointment, or action authority.
ambiguityNotes: Candidate does not mean approved baseline

invariants: Every governed mutation commits current state, immutable history, and audit evidence atomically
Every semantic read binds the exact current Product and Initiative

boundedContexts.name: Native Product Studio
boundedContexts.purpose: Own native human interaction and privacy-safe presentation while delegating governed Product semantics to the shared engine boundary.
responsibilities: Collect explicit human inputs through a native host surface
Render strict privacy-safe engine projections and bounded errors
excludedResponsibilities: Synthesize Product decisions, ownership acceptance, approval, or readiness

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A strict read model containing only declared identities, counts, statuses, timestamps, and digests needed for native Product inspection.
ambiguityNotes: A projection is not the governed source record

invariants: Host responses reject extra private fields and substituted bindings
Native presentation never grants Product or execution authority

contracts.name: Strict Product Studio engine protocol
contracts.versioning: The protocol uses an explicit version and rejects downgrade, unknown method, unexpected request fields, and incompatible response shape.
contracts.compatibility: Every supported native host must parse the exact response contract and reject binding, snapshot-digest, privacy-boundary, or authority-boundary drift.
contracts.consistency: The response binds one exact Product revision, Initiative revision, governed candidate record, assessment, and snapshot digest from a single read boundary.
contracts.failureBehavior: The consumer receives a bounded non-authorizing failure and must not display private payload details or retry a semantic mutation implicitly.

relationships.rationale: The native surface supplies explicit human intent and consumes strict shared-engine outcomes while the engine owns governed Product semantics.
relationships.changeCoordination: Protocol changes require shared contract review, four-host parser evidence, package rebinding, and no synthesized approval or migration authority.

governance.basis: Named roles prepare and challenge the candidate boundary and ownership trace, but a separate accountable human decision is required for approval and acceptance.

limitations: No organizational appointment, accepted ownership, approved boundary, readiness, release, deployment, or action authority is represented
